cweDef.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
cweDef.summary: A browser protection is present but not actually in force.

title: Permissions-Policy grants a powerful feature to every origin
description: The Permissions-Policy header contains a wildcard grant for a powerful feature such as camera, microphone or geolocation. Any embedded frame can then request the feature without the top-level document narrowing it, which is the opposite of what the header exists to do. The check reports the wildcard grant on one observation; it does not claim the feature is actually reachable.
remediation: Replace wildcard grants with an explicit allowlist of origins, or close the feature with an empty allowlist (camera=()).
limitation: Observation-level: the check reads the declared header text and does not evaluate how a browser applies the policy to a specific frame.
scopeT: One response: confirm a wildcard grant for a powerful feature.
fp: A deployment that intentionally delegates one feature to a trusted origin is reported only when the grant is a wildcard.
recordDesc: The response delegates a powerful feature to every origin. Permissions-Policy restricts which frames may use capabilities like the camera and microphone; a wildcard removes the restriction for any origin the page embeds. The header is increasingly common but is often copied with wildcards that were meant as placeholders.
applicability: HTML responses that deliver a Permissions-Policy header.
risk: Feature delegation to untrusted frames; LOW severity.
why: A powerful feature is granted to every origin.
fix: Close unused features with an empty allowlist.
verifyT: Re-observe the header and confirm no feature uses a wildcard grant.

cweDef.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
cweDef.summary: A browser protection is present but not actually in force.

title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy explicitly set to unsafe-none
description: The response sets Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy to unsafe-none, which is the value that disables the browsing-context separation the header otherwise provides. A document that opens or is opened by a cross-origin window keeps a live opener relationship, enabling window references across origins. The check reports the explicit value; the impact depends on what the page does with opener access.
remediation: Set Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy to same-origin, or same-origin-allow-popups where popups must keep a relationship.
limitation: Observation-level: whether the page relies on cross-origin opener access is a design question the header alone cannot answer.
scopeT: One response: confirm COOP is present with the unsafe-none value.
fp: A page whose documented design requires cross-origin window messaging is the accepted, reviewed exception.
recordDesc: The response explicitly opts out of cross-origin opener isolation. unsafe-none is the default in browsers that predate COOP, so setting it is equivalent to stating that cross-origin window references are wanted; it also defeats the isolation needed for cross-origin isolation features. A copied header template with the wrong value is the usual cause.
applicability: HTML responses that deliver a Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header.
risk: Cross-origin window reference exposure; LOW severity.
why: The policy explicitly disables opener isolation.
fix: Use same-origin-allow-popups where popups are required.
verifyT: Re-observe the header and confirm same-origin or same-origin-allow-popups.
